purpose: common-random-number causal attribution of uniform native strict-pass counts; no width refit

design.native_arms: A-D, all four arms share each replicate's truth/count-split/mark/posterior seeds

D_controls.native: D intensity discrepancy and gamma-Poisson overdispersion retained
D_controls.no_phi: D intensity discrepancy retained; D count generation and Fisher variance made Poisson
D_controls.no_discrepancy: D gamma-Poisson overdispersion retained; D intensity replaced by C intensity (RSD+FoG, no D discrepancy)
D_controls.no_phi_no_discrepancy: both D-specific overdispersion and discrepancy removed

interpretation.causal_rule: A D-specific mechanism is supported only if the paired D control changes coverage/pass behavior while common seeds and other interfaces remain fixed.
interpretation.conclusion: The common-seed factorial is informative but not a clean single-cause attribution: removing phi changes strict passes 1/16 to 2/16, removing the D discrepancy changes 1/16 to 0/16, and removing both remains 0/16. The controls alter different likelihood/data-generating interfaces and do not justify a D-only width or gate repair. Retain the no-attribution disposition and keep widths frozen.
interpretation.width_policy: diagnostic-only; no posterior width or mean-model refit
